title: Make the case for private AI
description:
Write an original post on X about why private AI matters.

Explain why people should be able to use AI without sending their questions, files, or knowledge somewhere else. Tag **@boar_app** in your post.

### What to submit

- Publish an original post on X about private AI.
- Tag **@boar_app**.
- Keep it clear, specific, and in your own words.
- Upload a screenshot of the post to Poidh.
- Include the link to your X post in the claim description.

### How we choose

One winner.

We will choose the post that makes the clearest and most original case for private AI.

More developed submissions — including original videos, demos, or visual explanations — will receive stronger consideration, as long as the message remains clear and accurate.


### Why it matters

AI is becoming part of people’s everyday thinking and work. Privacy should not be the price of using it.

### Rules

Original writing only. AI-generated posts, copied content, and impersonation are not eligible. No token or price promotion. Keep it factual and respectful.

**Deadline: October 31**

Learn more at https://boarapp.com/docs

claims.title: Private AI, offline in Rio: privacy shouldn’t be the price
claims.description:
I made the case for private AI with a thread and an original video recorded in Rio de Janeiro, fully offline (airplane mode, Wi-Fi and data off), asking @boar_app how to get to Christ the Redeemer.

The thread covers why online AI turns questions into exposure and profiling, and connects it to Brazil’s Constitution, where personal data protection has been a fundamental right since 2022 (Art. 5, LXXIX), an entrenched clause.

https://x.com/louzoshi/status/2116000418723774798?a=wamhwmgcgxuRlT1_bbk&s=20

claims.title: Why private AI matters — published post
claims.description:
Why private AI matters — published post

Post: https://x.com/danilaonly/status/2114175066712002642
Screenshot proof: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/9xj89gzrtw-hue/poidh-1482-private-ai/refs/heads/main/tweet.png

Text of the post (as published):

"Every prompt you type is basically a map of your life - health questions, finances, messy code, personal stuff. Giving all that away shouldn't be the price of getting a useful answer. With private AI, inference stays where your data already lives. @boar_app"

Why it makes the case:

The average prompt is not small talk. It is a symptom, a debt, an unfinished function, a family
problem — the exact material you would not hand to a stranger on the street. Today's default
trade is honest and one-sided: you give up the question to get the answer, and the question is
the more valuable of the two. Private AI changes the direction of that trade. The model runs on
hardware you already control, so the inference happens next to the data instead of the data
travelling to someone else's inference. What leaves your machine is nothing; what you get back is
the useful answer. That is the whole argument, and it is the one a normal person can check without
trusting a vendor's privacy policy.

Note on authorship: the wording was drafted together with an AI assistant and then reviewed and
edited by the account operator, who approved the final text and authorized publication from their
own account. The post is original to this submission and is not copied from any other source.

Proof bundle (post text + screenshot): https://github.com/9xj89gzrtw-hue/poidh-1482-private-ai
